newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields rise with other Europeans.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields rise with other Europeans.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were dragged higher on Monday while the crown strengthened marginally.
"We followed a small recoil abroad. German bond yields were up in a slight recoil and partly due to a big issue of German 30-year bonds later on this week," one dealer said.
Statistics from the U.S., the Chicago purchasers index and new home sales for May, also contributed to the rise in Swedish bond yields, dealers said.
An auction of two billion crowns worth of 10 year bonds on Wednesday could also have been a reason for the rise.
"I think it will be hard to buy the 1037 (10 year) bond at these levels. I think we'll have to the 6.70 percent level to find buyers," one dealer said.
The difference between Swedish and German 10-year bond yields decreased by two basis points to 93.
Dealers said the generally stronger trend in Sweden seemed to be continuing. Moody's positive comments about Sweden last week might be continuing to give support.
The ten-year debt yield rose two basis points to 6.64 percent while the six-month T-bill rate was flat at 4.13 percent.
The crown rose marginally to 4.4375 against the mark from 4.4440 late on Friday, mainly due to a weaker mark.

The market was now focusing on the FOMC-meeting that starts on Tuesday and U.S. statistics later in the week such as non-farm payrolls on Thursday and NAPM on Tuesday. One dealer said a German auction of 30-year bonds on Wednesday will also be important. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019
